apps.name: Tuna
apps.subtitle: Your music at home.
apps.localizedDescription: Your music from your Tuna server, with mixes and lyrics. Download songs to play offline.

versions.localizedDescription:
New
- Import your own files: a song Get couldn't find, an album, or anything you have. On a song or album that wasn't found, its button now offers Look again or Import files; Your library has Import files for anything. Choose the files (on a computer, a whole folder) and a cover if you like (a folder's cover.jpg is used by itself). The files are sent, then shown with their names filled in, from the song or album asked for, what MusicBrainz knows (titles, track numbers, year) and their tags, for you to change: artist, album, year, and each song's number, title and artist. Then Lidarr files them into the album when it knows it, or Tuna puts them straight into the music folder. Files that don't play are turned away, and so are songs whose length is more than 10 seconds off the album's, or that are in the library already, each with why.
- Songs Soulseek seems not to have are looked for again in other ways: some names (Kanye West's, for one) get no answer at all on Soulseek, so when the first search finds nothing that fits, Tuna searches by the title and the album, then by the title and one word of the artist's name.

Changed
- Playlists show where each missing song is at: the + with its circle going round while it's looked for, then a quiet + when it wasn't found.
- The log says why a song wasn't found on Soulseek: how many people answered and why none fit (without the title, without the artist, the wrong length).

Fixed
- Missing songs in playlists always showed Get, even while being looked for or after they weren't found.

To update: the server (pull the new image), and in Tuna's stack add the data folder as Lidarr has it,
- ${DATA_BASE_PATH}:/data, to its volumes (Importing files needs it; Settings → Connections says if
Tuna can't reach Lidarr's music folder). The apps: on a Mac a whole folder can be chosen, on Android
several files at once.
